news.headline: Pope Leo XIV thanks wellwishers in first event after cancer surgery
news.story_lead: Pope Leo XIV thanks wellwishers in first event after cancer surgery Pope Leo XIV held his first public engagement since his lung cancer surgery on Sunday, as he recited the Angelus prayer from the window of Vatican's Apostolic Palace. The surgery had taken place just a few days before, after Pope Leo had been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer. After the prayer, he thanked the people who have prayed for him in recent days and said he appreciated the support.

news.headline: Rain lashes Chennai as northeast monsoon gets active in Tamil Nadu; roads flooded, traffic snarls | Visuals
news.story_lead: Rain lashes Chennai as northeast monsoon gets active in Tamil Nadu; roads flooded, traffic snarls | Visuals The IMD forecasts widespread rainfall across Tamil Nadu, with very heavy rain possible until October 21 and a yellow alert in effect through October 23. Heavy rainfall pounded Tamil Nadu's Chennai as the northeast monsoon intensified, triggered severe waterlogging and traffic congestion in several parts of the city. The rain continued through the night up to Sunday morning, causing flooding of several roads across the city, particularly in North Chennai , where it became difficult for the residents to commute.
news.full_article_text: Rain lashes Chennai as northeast monsoon gets active in Tamil Nadu; roads flooded, traffic snarls | Visuals The IMD forecasts widespread rainfall across Tamil Nadu, with very heavy rain possible until October 21 and a yellow alert in effect through October 23. Heavy rainfall pounded Tamil Nadu's Chennai as the northeast monsoon intensified, triggered severe waterlogging and traffic congestion in several parts of the city. The rain continued through the night up to Sunday morning, causing flooding of several roads across the city, particularly in North Chennai , where it became difficult for the residents to commute. North Chennai bore the initial strain of the showers, recording between 6 cm and 10 cm of rainfall in less than an hour. Videos shared by news agencies ANI and PTI display heavy rains and flooding in the city and residential areas. Chennai locals also shared videos on X expressing agitation over the weather. Also Read | Southwest monsoon withdraws from entire country: IMD One X user shared a view of Chennai airport enveloped in heavy rain, showcasing light flooding on the ramp. Chennai steps up preparedness The flooding has prompted civic authorities in Chennai to step up preparedness. More than 15,000 sanitation and other civic workers were deployed across the city overnight to clear flooded roads, manage waterlogging and respond to complaints. The Tamil Nadu State Disaster Response Force also deployed 100 personnel as a precaution, with National Disaster Response Force and State Disaster Response Force teams being mobilised to assist if conditions worsen. Also Read | Mercury drops in Delhi after rainfall, AQI down to ‘satisfactory’ level Northeast monsoon intensifies The heavy rainfall follows the onset of the northeast monsoon over Tamil Nadu, which started on October 17, according to IMD. The northeast monsoon (often called the winter or retreating monsoon) is a seasonal wind and rainfall pattern that occurs from October to December in the South Asian peninsula. The seasonal rain is particularly significant for Tamil Nadu, which depends heavily on the northeast monsoon for its annual rainfall. The showers were triggered by a cyclonic circulation over north Tamil Nadu and coastal Andhra Pradesh, along with a trough stretching from Lakshadweep towards the southwest Bay of Bengal. Heavy rainfall to continue The IMD has issued a yellow alert until 23 October, with very heavy rain lasting until 21 October, across the state. A yellow alert means heavy rainfall between 6 cm and 11 cm. Flooded roads may lead to prolonged traffic congestions, particularly in low-lying areas. Meteorologists forecast that widespread rainfall will continue across several districts -- Chennai, Chengalpattu, Tiruvallur, Kancheepuram, Villupuram, Cuddalore, Mayiladuthurai, Nagapattinam, Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Pudukkottai, Ramanathapuram, Sivaganga, Thoothukudi, Kallakurichi, Ariyalur, Perambalur, Tiruchirappalli, Nilgiris, Coimbatore and Tirunelveli. Heavy showers could lead to temporary waterlogging, slower traffic and disruption to daily activities, particularly in locations with poor drainage. The RMC has issued an advisory on X regarding Do's and Don'ts for severe thunderstorm-like conditions, highlighting preparations and responses for different situations, including what one should do if struck by lightning. Residents are advised exercise caution while travelling through waterlogged areas and avoid crossing flooded roads. People should also take shelter indoors during thunderstorms and stay away from exposed locations during lightning activity. news.headline: Rajnath Singh to represent India at SCO Meet in Tajikistan, focus on trade, connectivity and regional cooperation
news.story_lead: Rajnath Singh to represent India at SCO Meet in Tajikistan, focus on trade, connectivity and regional cooperation As per Ministry of Defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO Member States. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Tajikistan's Dushanbe to represent India at the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (CHG) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation ( SCO ), scheduled to be held on October 19 to October 20. According to the Ministry of Defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO Member States, particularly in the areas of trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges.

The meeting will provide an opportunity for India to exchange views with other SCO Member States on advancing practical and mutually beneficial cooperation within the Organisation. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will visit Tajikistan's Dushanbe to represent India at the 25th Meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (CHG) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation ( SCO ), scheduled to be held on October 19 to October 20.

According to the Ministry of Defence, the meeting will focus on strengthening multilateral cooperation among SCO Member States, particularly in the areas of trade, economy, investment, connectivity, innovation and cultural-humanitarian exchanges.
ALSO READ: Rajnath, Yogi finalise plan to prevent flooding along Gomti
It is also expected to review the progress of ongoing cooperation initiatives and consider decisions relating to the Organisation's financial and institutional functioning, it added.

news.headline: Tamil Nadu: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes
news.story_lead: Tamil Nadu: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes Ranipet , Veteran Tamil music composer and singer Deva, popularly known as 'Thenisai Thendral', was laid to rest with full state honours at his family farmland in Sakkaramallur near Arcot, Ranipet district, on Sunday. Deva died of a heart attack in Chennai on the morning of October 17. His mortal remains were taken from his Chennai residence to the farmland, where the final rites were performed.
news.full_article_text: Tamil Nadu: ‘Thenisai Thendral’ Deva laid to rest amid tears, tributes Ranipet , Veteran Tamil music composer and singer Deva, popularly known as 'Thenisai Thendral', was laid to rest with full state honours at his family farmland in Sakkaramallur near Arcot, Ranipet district, on Sunday. Deva died of a heart attack in Chennai on the morning of October 17. His mortal remains were taken from his Chennai residence to the farmland, where the final rites were performed. Thousands of people gathered at the site to pay their last respects to the celebrated music director. Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay had visited Deva's residence in Chennai to pay his respects and announced that the funeral would be held with state honours in recognition of the composer's contribution to the music industry. Revenue and police officials oversaw arrangements for the ceremony at Sakkaramallur. Relatives and villagers recalled Deva's enduring connection to his roots, saying he regularly visited his native village during festivals such as Pongal and contributed to local initiatives, including funding the construction of a Sri Ranganathar temple. Born Devanesan Chokkalingam, Deva had a career spanning nearly four decades and composed music for more than 400 films in Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Malayalam. Before turning to films, Deva was an employee of the Tamil Nadu government's Public Works Department . He made his entry as a composer in 1986 with 'Mattukkara Mannaru', which did not fare well in theatres, though its songs found a loyal audience over time. 'Manasukketha Maharasa' , starring Ramarajan and Seetha, was the film that first drew attention to his work. His real breakthrough, however, came in 1990 with the Prashanth-starrer 'Vaigasi Poranthachu', which won him widespread acclaim. Deva rose to prominence in the late 1980s and 1990s with his high-energy, folk-rooted tunes, and is widely credited with bringing the 'gaana' genre into mainstream Tamil cinema. Few composers in Tamil cinema are as closely identified with one genre as Deva is with 'gaana', the urban folk music born in the working-class neighbourhoods of North Chennai. He worked with nearly every leading star of his time, among them Vijayakanth, Sarathkumar, Vijay and Ajith, and delivered some of the biggest hits of their careers. Among his chartbusters were the Rajinikanth films 'Annamalai', 'Baashha' and 'Arunachalam', and the Kamal Haasan outings 'Avvai Shanmugi', 'Pammal K Sambandam' and 'Panchathanthiram'. His death drew tributes from political leaders, members of the film fraternity and fans across Tamil Nadu. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

news.exam_corner_topic: CJI announces virtual access to Supreme Court for Leh, Kargil lawyers
news.headline: CJI announces virtual access to Supreme Court for Leh, Kargil lawyers
news.story_lead: CJI announces virtual access to Supreme Court for Leh, Kargil lawyers The CJI spoke of a young child studying in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra who might one day argue a case before the court or even serve as a judge on its bench. Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on Sunday said lawyers from Leh and Kargil would soon be able to virtually access the Supreme Court from the Ladakh Bench of the High Court. All matters originating from Ladakh would be listed on a single day and heard through video-conferencing, sparing lawyers and litigants the time, cost and hardship of travelling to Delhi, Justice Kant said as he inaugurated the Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh here.
news.full_article_text: CJI announces virtual access to Supreme Court for Leh, Kargil lawyers The CJI spoke of a young child studying in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra who might one day argue a case before the court or even serve as a judge on its bench. Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on Sunday said lawyers from Leh and Kargil would soon be able to virtually access the Supreme Court from the Ladakh Bench of the High Court. All matters originating from Ladakh would be listed on a single day and heard through video-conferencing, sparing lawyers and litigants the time, cost and hardship of travelling to Delhi, Justice Kant said as he inaugurated the Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh here. Describing the inauguration as a historic step, the CJI referred to the establishment of a Special Court in Leh in 1870, observing that while the institution had passed into history, the geographical challenges that restricted access to justice persisted for generations. "For close to a century, the high court that served Ladakh sat beyond the Great Himalayas, reachable in winter only by air," he said. The CJI said the insertion of the name 'Ladakh' in a high court after it became a Union Territory in 2019 was an important step, but the gesture remained largely symbolic. "A name on a court's letterhead is not the same as a court at one's doorstep," he said. Also Read: ‘Children have a fundamental right to internet access, blanket bans disproportionate’: Supreme Court Justice Kant emphasised that the bench belongs equally to Leh and Kargil – the two districts in the Union Territory - and said its purpose would be served only when people in every corner of Ladakh start to feel a sense of ownership over the institution. He also said that once video-conferencing facilities have been set up at the bench, the Supreme Court would list all matters originating from Ladakh on a single day and hear them on a day-to-day basis virtually. The arrangement, the CJI said, would enable members of the Leh and Kargil bar associations to argue cases before the top court without leaving Ladakh. "In this way, the distance will no longer stand between people of Ladakh and the highest Court of our country," he said. Justice Kant said that the true measure of a court is not its geographical elevation but its accessibility to the people it serves. "We are some 3,500 metres above the sea, and I am told no high court in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves," he said. Also Read: Supreme Court panel opens portal for complaints over violence on July 20 Delhi protest The CJI recalled the role of village institutions and customary practices in resolving disputes, noting that the region had long relied on community-based mechanisms to uphold fairness and settle grievances. On improving access to justice, he identified technology and legal aid as two essential instruments for overcoming geographical barriers. "In a land of such vast distances, technology can do what no road ever could," he said. The CJI also underlined the importance of legal aid, calling it a constitutional promise that no citizen should be denied justice because of poverty or disability. He stressed the need for legal awareness camps, para-legal volunteers, affordable legal representation, lok adalats and timely compensation for victims of crime. "Access to justice, after all, begins not in the court's compound, but at the litigant's door," he said, expressing confidence that the Ladakh Legal Services Authority and the court's Legal Services Committee would work together to reach people awaiting justice in remote areas. "When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh, but taken root here," Justice Kant said.

It was a showman’s reveal, built for the livestream. Nearly eight years earlier, an engineer in Maranello had drawn up a Ferrari that used the same sort of jets for a different purpose, to sharpen its driving dynamics by pressing the car into the road so it could corner, brake and accelerate harder. Ferrari chief executive Benedetto Vigna confirmed the design in an interview with Hindustan Times in New Delhi, where the Italian supercar maker on Saturday unveiled the Luce, its first all-electric car, and brought its Universo Ferrari exhibition to India for the first time. news.story_lead: Delhi court convicts man for shooting at wife outside hospital where she worked as security guard New Delhi, A Delhi court has convicted a man for attempting to murder his wife by shooting her in the stomach outside a hospital in Connaught Place in 2018, saying the testimony of the injured woman was credible, trustworthy and sufficient to establish his guilt. The court, however, acquitted him of the charge under Section 25 of the Arms Act, which relates to illegal possession of a firearm.
news.full_article_text: Delhi court convicts man for shooting at wife outside hospital where she worked as security guard New Delhi, A Delhi court has convicted a man for attempting to murder his wife by shooting her in the stomach outside a hospital in Connaught Place in 2018, saying the testimony of the injured woman was credible, trustworthy and sufficient to establish his guilt. Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana, in a judgment dated October 13, held Sushant guilty under IPC Section 307 and Section 27 of the Arms Act, which deals with the use of arms. The court, however, acquitted him of the charge under Section 25 of the Arms Act, which relates to illegal possession of a firearm. It noted that a separate FIR for possession of the pistol was registered at Seelampur police station, and the trial in that case is pending before another court. According to the prosecution, the incident took place on November 24, 2018, outside Gate No. 5 of Kalawati Hospital in Connaught Place. The victim, Pinki, worked as a security guard at the hospital and had been living at her parental home since her husband was sent to jail in a separate case in 2015. Pinki told the court that Sushant, who had been released from jail about a month and a half earlier, came to the hospital in the evening and called her outside. As she sat in an auto-rickshaw he had parked across the road, he asked whether she would return to her matrimonial home. When she refused, he fired a shot that hit her in the stomach and fled. The victim said she was operated upon the same day, remained hospitalised for about a month, and underwent four surgeries in a short span. The court said the evidence of the hospital staff, along with CCTV camera footage, established that the accused had come to the hospital and left with the victim shortly before she returned injured. It noted that the owner of an auto-rickshaw testified that he had handed the vehicle to Sushant that day, and the vehicle was found abandoned near the spot with blood stains, and that later a forensic analysis matched the blood sample collected from the vehicle with the victim's DNA. Citing several Supreme Court precedents, the court said the testimony of an injured witness carries great weight, as it comes with an inbuilt guarantee of presence at the scene, and that a conviction can rest on a single reliable witness. The court said the defence failed to point to any reason why Pinki would falsely implicate her husband, beyond a "bald suggestion" of false implication arising from a matrimonial dispute. "The accused fired upon the vital part of the body of the victim and, needless to say, he intended to eliminate the victim as she was not ready to live with the accused. "Hence, the prosecution is successful in proving beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had attempted to commit murder of his wife Pinki and he stands convicted under Section 307 of the IPC," the judge said. "I am of the considered view that the prosecution has successfully proved its case based on credible and trustworthy testimony of prosecution witness Pinki," he added. The arguments on sentencing will be heard on a later date. This article was generated from an automated news agency feed without modifications to text.

news.story_lead: Just Like That | Jantar Mantar: From the science of the stars to the politics of dissent Built in 1724 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, Delhi’s Jantar Mantar evolved from an astronomical observatory into a landmark of protest and political dissent. news.full_article_text: Just Like That | Jantar Mantar: From the science of the stars to the politics of dissent Built in 1724 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, Delhi’s Jantar Mantar evolved from an astronomical observatory into a landmark of protest and political dissent. Jantar Mantar in New Delhi is much in the news today, but how many of us are aware of its history? A monument conceived to measure the movements of celestial bodies has become a place where citizens seek to measure the distance between the promises of the state and the realities of their lives. Built to interrogate the heavens, it has become a forum for interrogating those who govern us. Its history is a reminder that monuments do not remain imprisoned in the purposes for which they were constructed. They acquire new meanings as the societies around them change. Jantar Mantar was built in 1724 by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur, a ruler whose interests extended well beyond the conventional preoccupations of kingship. Fascinated by mathematics and astronomy, Jai Singh was dissatisfied with the astronomical instruments available to him. He believed that their limitations compromised the accuracy of celestial observations. He therefore commissioned the construction of massive masonry instruments, designed to measure the positions and movements of heavenly bodies with greater precision. Delhi's observatory was the first of five that he established, the others being at Jaipur, Ujjain, Varanasi and Mathura. What makes Jantar Mantar remarkable is not merely its antiquity, but the intellectual ambition it embodies. The Samrat Yantra, an immense sundial, was designed to determine local time. The Jai Prakash Yantra used hemispherical structures to establish the positions of celestial objects, while the Ram Yantra helped measure their altitude and azimuth. Each structure translated an abstract mathematical problem into a tangible instrument. By enlarging the instruments and constructing them in durable masonry, Jai Singh sought to reduce errors of observation and obtain more dependable astronomical measurements. The observations made at Delhi contributed to the preparation of the Zij Muhammad Shahi, a set of astronomical tables intended to improve the calculation of celestial positions. Was this a breakthrough for its time? The answer requires a distinction. European astronomy had already been transformed by the telescope and by developments in heliocentric theory. Jai Singh's instruments largely belonged to the older tradition of positional astronomy, which relied on naked-eye observations and mathematical calculation. Their achievement lay in improving that tradition, not in replacing it with an entirely new understanding of the universe. The tragedy is that the growth of the modern city, the construction of surrounding buildings and the difficulty of preserving the instruments under their original observational conditions have compromised their astronomical utility. Yet Jantar Mantar has not become irrelevant. It has acquired another life. That transformation began decisively in 1993. Delhi's traditional arena for large public demonstrations had been the Boat Club lawns near India Gate, close to Parliament and the principal government offices. The enormous farmers' agitation led by Mahendra Singh Tikait in 1988 was held there. As governments sought to regulate such gatherings, the Boat Club became increasingly restricted. Jantar Mantar emerged as an alternative, more manageable venue for demonstrations. For more than three decades**,** Jantar Mantar has been a recurring destination for those who wanted to be heard by the government. In 2011, Anna Hazare's anti-corruption hunger strike helped ignite the India Against Corruption movement, which subsequently contributed to the emergence of the Aam Aadmi Party. Tamil Nadu farmers came to Delhi in 2017 to draw attention to agrarian distress and mounting debt. In December 2019, demonstrators opposed the Citizenship Amendment Act. In 2023, leading Indian wrestlers, including Vinesh Phogat, Sakshi Malik and Bajrang Punia, protested against Wrestling Federation of India chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, raising allegations of sexual harassment and demanding accountability. Students, workers, farmers, political parties, civil-society groups and individuals pursuing causes of public concern have all used the venue. These protests did not belong to one political party or ideological persuasion. Governments of different political complexions have faced demonstrations there. Of course, the right to protest cannot mean the right to inconvenience everyone without limit. In October 2017, the National Green Tribunal ordered a halt to protests at Jantar Mantar, citing concerns including noise, pollution and public inconvenience. In July 2018, the Supreme Court rejected a blanket prohibition, emphasising the need to balance the rights of residents with the constitutional freedoms of peaceful assembly and expression. There is, however, a new and significant development. On October 12, 2026, Delhi Police withdrew Jantar Mantar's status as a designated protest venue, naming Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi as alternatives. The decision has already been challenged in the Supreme Court and Delhi High Court. Thus, as this column is written, the future of Jantar Mantar as an officially designated site for dissent is contested. This brings us back to the monument itself. A monument built to measure the heavens has become a place where a democracy measures itself. Whether Jantar Mantar continues officially as a protest site or is replaced by more distant venues, the question it poses—what is the truth?—will remain. Pavan K Varma is an author, diplomat, and former member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha). The views expressed are personal

news.headline: Delhi Police lodge 3 FIRs over CJP's Tiranga march; Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora released
news.story_lead: Delhi Police lodge 3 FIRs over CJP's Tiranga march; Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora released The FIRs, filed at Connaught Place and Mandi House under Section 223 of the BNS for disobeying a lawful order, accuse protesters of defying prohibitory orders Delhi Police on Saturday lodged at least three FIRs over Friday’s Tiranga march, naming Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders among others, and released Dipke after nearly 24 hours in custody and a bond to keep the peace for a year, as protesters gathered outside police headquarters demanded cases against officers they accused of assaulting them. The FIRs, filed at Connaught Place and Mandi House under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for disobeying a lawful order, accuse protesters of defying prohibitory orders, marching in
news.full_article_text: Delhi Police lodge 3 FIRs over CJP's Tiranga march; Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora released The FIRs, filed at Connaught Place and Mandi House under Section 223 of the BNS for disobeying a lawful order, accuse protesters of defying prohibitory orders Delhi Police on Saturday lodged at least three FIRs over Friday’s Tiranga march, naming Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, All India Students’ Association (AISA) president Neha Bora and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leaders among others, and released Dipke after nearly 24 hours in custody and a bond to keep the peace for a year, as protesters gathered outside police headquarters demanded cases against officers they accused of assaulting them. The FIRs, filed at Connaught Place and Mandi House under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for disobeying a lawful order, accuse protesters of defying prohibitory orders, marching in the middle of roads and obstructing police. Police had already taken down the names, addresses and phone numbers of those detained on Friday, and on Friday evening, made some of them sign notices to join the investigation, HT has learnt. The notice, issued under Section 35(3) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) for cases in which police choose not to arrest, cites FIR 294/26, registered at Connaught Place police station on October 16 under Section 223(a) read with Section 3(5), the BNS provision on acts done with common intention. Deep Dive “Although you are not being placed under arrest at this stage in respect of the aforesaid FIR, you are directed to comply with all of the following conditions,” it says, binding the signatory not to commit any offence, tamper with evidence or threaten anyone acquainted with the case, and to appear in court when directed. More FIRs were being filed, police said, and footage from CCTV cameras and social media was being used to identify those who marched on the inner circle of Connaught Place. Dipke was released at around 4.45pm on Saturday after being produced before a special executive magistrate at Mandir Marg police station, where proceedings scheduled for noon were delayed by almost five hours. Police said he had been arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the BNSS, which provide for preventive action, and that his attempt to join the march breached the bond he signed on October 11, after he and co-convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were detained aboard a flight at Delhi airport. Also Read | Abhijeet Dipke, Neha Bora among 150 detained in Delhi; Oppn slams police action amid anti-CEC protests Police had picked Dipke up outside a friend’s house in Jhandewalan around 4.40pm on Friday, after serving him a notice barring him from the march. “I am alone. Why are you stopping me?” he asked, unfurling the tricolour before he was pushed into a van, and the CJP alleged he was moved between several police stations in Dwarka and southwest Delhi, denied his phone and kept from a lawyer. Bora was released at 6am after about 12 hours at RK Puram police station, detained under Section 65 of the Delhi Police Act, a senior officer said. AISA alleged that police dragged, shoved and beat Bora and her associates at Mandi House and kept her lawyer away through the night, which police refused to comment on. “By what law is it permissible to keep detainees all night long?” Bora asked. Police are also seeking a woman who, in a nine-second video they released, is seen slapping a woman paramilitary officer during a scuffle near Palika Bazaar, and said they would act against protesters who jumped barricades on Sansad Marg and against AAP, whose leaders Sanjay Singh and Saurabh Bhardwaj led a march near Rashtrapati Bhavan on Friday. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jignasa Sinha Jignasa Sinha is a Special Correspondent at Hindustan Times in New Delhi. With more than six years of reporting experience, she covers crime and policing in the national capital. Her beats also include Delhi prisons, the Delhi Fire Services and Delhi courts, while she regularly reports on gender, labour and social justice. Over the course of her career, Jignasa has reported on major criminal investigations, international crime syndicates, high-profile cyber fraud cases, law-and-order developments, protests, disasters and public institutions. Her reporting combines breaking news with in-depth, long form, human interest stories that examine the human impact of public policy, policing and the criminal justice system. In addition to reporting for the newspaper, she contributes to the Hindustan Times website and app, and plays an active role in coordinating on-ground coverage of major developments and breaking news across Delhi. Before joining Hindustan Times, Jignasa worked at The Indian Express newspaper in New Delhi, where she spent five years covering crime, Delhi airport, courts and health. She began her journalism career as an intern at an AI magazine in Bengaluru while pursuing her postgraduate diploma in multimedia journalism at the Indian Institute of Journalism and New Media. news.headline: One person with alleged terror links arrested, says K'taka Home Minister
news.story_lead: One person with alleged terror links arrested, says K'taka Home Minister Kalaburagi , Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday said one person has been arrested here for allegedly having links with terror groups through social media, while further investigation was underway against the other. Two youths, both originally from outside Karnataka, came under the scanner following a joint operation by the central agencies and the state government's Internal Security Division, he said. "In a joint operation by the central government and the state government's internal security division, on receiving information that two youths were developing links with terrorists through social media, they were detained," Kharge told reporters.
news.full_article_text: One person with alleged terror links arrested, says K'taka Home Minister Kalaburagi , Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge on Sunday said one person has been arrested here for allegedly having links with terror groups through social media, while further investigation was underway against the other. Two youths, both originally from outside Karnataka, came under the scanner following a joint operation by the central agencies and the state government's Internal Security Division, he said. "In a joint operation by the central government and the state government's internal security division, on receiving information that two youths were developing links with terrorists through social media, they were detained," Kharge told reporters. Following the investigation, it was established that one of them was in regular contact with the suspected terror network, while the other was not in contact with anyone in this regard, he said. "We have arrested one person, and further investigation is underway against the other," the minister said. Kharge said this was the fifth such case reported in the last two to three months, adding that the individuals involved were from Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and West Bengal. "We have taken this seriously. We are combing through social media and other activities of migrant workers. We will not take this lightly and will take necessary action in coordination with the Government of India," he said. On migrant workers moving to Karnataka in search of employment, the home minister said the government could not prevent people from coming to the state to earn a livelihood, as it was their constitutional right. However, he urged employers to verify the backgrounds of people they hire. "We have repeatedly told coffee plantation owners, construction contractors, factories, textile mills, quick-commerce and e-commerce companies to approach us for verification. news.headline: Sahyog Portal could detect, remove child abuse material: Supreme Court
news.story_lead: Sahyog Portal could detect, remove child abuse material: Supreme Court “Our expectations from the portal, however, are much more than what it is, as of now, capable of doing, and we are hopeful that the Union of India shares the same vision,” it said. news.full_article_text: Sahyog Portal could detect, remove child abuse material: Supreme Court “Our expectations from the portal, however, are much more than what it is, as of now, capable of doing, and we are hopeful that the Union of India shares the same vision,” it said. The Supreme Court has said the Union government’s Sahyog Portal can provide the “foundation for a national database to detect and remove child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) across online platforms”. The observation comes as the portal itself faces legal challenges before the Supreme Court and several high courts and the court has called for “coordinated mechanisms to detect and remove” CSEAM from online platforms. In its order passed on October 15, a bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the Sahyog Portal could provide the “foundation for such a database”. The database will contain verified digital fingerprints, known as hashes, and URLs of CSEAM, allowing intermediaries to identify and remove known material across platforms. “We acknowledge that the Sahyog Portal is, no doubt, a step in the right direction. It is also not lost on us that the portal, by virtue of having already onboarded a considerable number of intermediaries, may well be the natural foundation upon which a Hash & URL List Database could be built,” the Supreme Court said. The court added that it was aware that the Sahyog portal currently worked only as a common platform for routing individual reports and takedown notices, and so it acts on CSEAM only when each instance is reported. However, the portal could do much more, the court said as long as the Union government “shared its vision” with that of the court’s expressed in the present order. To prevent wrongful takedowns, the court said each entry must undergo multiple levels of verification, with at least three trained human analysts independently confirming that the material constitutes CSEAM. The database must store only digital identifiers and URLs, not the material itself, and authorities must maintain audit records and correct erroneous entries. The court said the existing system relied heavily on individual complaints and separate detection mechanisms maintained by platforms. As a result, removing material from one platform did not ensure its removal elsewhere, allowing it to continue circulating across the internet. It, however, directed the Union government to frame guidelines and standard operating procedures to strengthen the detection, removal and reporting of CSEAM, including through amendments to the Information Technology Act and IT Rules, wherever necessary. Platforms must promptly remove material that matches a verified database entry and provide users with a notice explaining the basis for removal, the Court said. It also called for an accessible grievance-redressal mechanism, with a distinct category for CSEAM complaints that users can reach within two steps from the content, profile, group or link concerned. Grievance officers must receive regular training to identify such material, including content that may not appear explicit on its face. The Court said intermediaries must report CSEAM to Indian law enforcement authorities, including the Special Juvenile Police Unit and local police, rather than merely reporting it to foreign organisations. Material of unknown origin removed following a complaint must be reported within two hours of resolving the complaint. Platforms must also report removals made through their own detection mechanisms or following a court or government direction within two hours of removal. Database-match removals must feature in consolidated weekly reports. The constitutional validity of the Sahyog portal has been challenged by several parties including the social media platform X corp. In September last year, a single bench of the Karnataka high court had upheld the constitutional validity of the portal. X Corp had then challenged the single judge’s order. The Supreme Court subsequently stayed a batch of such proceedings against Sahyog, including the appeal pending before the Karnataka high court and two pleas pending before the Bombay high court, including one filed by stand up comedian Kunal Kamra, challenging the constitutional validity of the central content-takedown mechanism. The court halted these proceedings in August following a transfer petition filed by the Union government that was seeking to consolidate all parallel challenges into a single, unified adjudication before the apex court to prevent conflicting judicial rulings on the intersection of the portal, Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, and online freedom of speech. It directed platforms to examine the broader context of advertisements and links, including captions, keywords and the purpose of tools being promoted. Their obligations may extend to advertisements for applications that manipulate children’s photographs into sexually exploitative material and links that redirect users to websites hosting such content. It asked the government to consider “exemplary” monetary penalties “proportionate to the gravity and recurrence of violations”, as well as an intermediary’s size and turnover. It also called for the disgorgement of revenue earned from CSEAM circulated through paywalls or subscriptions, in addition to applicable fines. It directed the government to file an affidavit detailing progress towards compliance by the next hearing on December 10, 2026. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ayesha Arvind Ayesha Arvind is a Senior Assistant Editor specialising in legal and judicial reportage. She covers High Courts and tribunals across southern India, and believes that important legal developments do not only come from New Delhi. Her work focuses on bringing significant decisions and developments from the region to a wider audience and explaining what they mean beyond the courtroom. She tries to make legal material accessible by translating legal jargon into clear, readable prose and putting pleas, lawsuits, judgments and legal developments in context. She also looks at their political realities and practical consequences for people. Ayesha is committed to the standards of integrity journalism requires. She places a premium on accuracy and fairness, and believes that journalism's powerful voice must be tempered by humility and a sense of proportion. Over almost two decades in journalism, she has covered law and order, civil law, crime and other areas of legal affairs. Her work includes breaking news, legal affairs stories, online analysis and commentary. Ayesha is deeply interested in the law, court judgments and the Constitution because they shape everyday life. The Supreme Court subsequently stayed a batch of such proceedings against Sahyog, including the appeal pending before the Karnataka high court and two pleas pending before the Bombay high court, including one filed by stand up comedian Kunal Kamra, challenging the constitutional validity of the central content-takedown mechanism. The court halted these proceedings in August following a transfer petition filed by the Union government that was seeking to consolidate all parallel challenges into a single, unified adjudication before the apex court to prevent conflicting judicial rulings on the intersection of the portal, Section 79(3)(b) of the IT Act, and online freedom of speech. It directed platforms to examine the broader context of advertisements and links, including captions, keywords and the purpose of tools being promoted. Their obligations may extend to advertisements for applications that manipulate children’s photographs into sexually exploitative material and links that redirect users to websites hosting such content. It asked the government to consider “exemplary” monetary penalties “proportionate to the gravity and recurrence of violations”, as well as an intermediary’s size and turnover. It also called for the disgorgement of revenue earned from CSEAM circulated through paywalls or subscriptions, in addition to applicable fines. It directed the government to file an affidavit detailing progress towards compliance by the next hearing on December 10, 2026. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Ayesha Arvind Ayesha Arvind is a Senior Assistant Editor specialising in legal and judicial reportage. She covers High Courts and tribunals across southern India, and believes that important legal developments do not only come from New Delhi. Her work focuses on bringing significant decisions and developments from the region to a wider audience and explaining what they mean beyond the courtroom. She tries to make legal material accessible by translating legal jargon into clear, readable prose and putting pleas, lawsuits, judgments and legal developments in context. She also looks at their political realities and practical consequences for people. Ayesha is committed to the standards of integrity journalism requires. She places a premium on accuracy and fairness, and believes that journalism's powerful voice must be tempered by humility and a sense of proportion. Over almost two decades in journalism, she has covered law and order, civil law, crime and other areas of legal affairs. Her work includes breaking news, legal affairs stories, online analysis and commentary. Ayesha is deeply interested in the law, court judgments and the Constitution because they shape everyday life. She believes every citizen should have a basic understanding of them. What she enjoys most about covering courts is that every story brings something new to learn. Read More
bullet_points: Sahyog Portal could detect, remove child abuse material: Supreme Court
“Our expectations from the portal, however, are much more than what it is, as of now, capable of doing, and we are hopeful that the Union of India shares the same vision,” it said.

The Supreme Court has said the Union government’s Sahyog Portal can provide the “foundation for a national database to detect and remove child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) across online platforms”.

The observation comes as the portal itself faces legal challenges before the Supreme Court and several high courts and the court has called for “coordinated mechanisms to detect and remove” CSEAM from online platforms.

In its order passed on October 15, a bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the Sahyog Portal could provide the “foundation for such a database”. The database will contain verified digital fingerprints, known as hashes, and URLs of CSEAM, allowing intermediaries to identify and remove known material across platforms.

“We acknowledge that the Sahyog Portal is, no doubt, a step in the right direction. It is also not lost on us that the portal, by virtue of having already onboarded a considerable number of intermediaries, may well be the natural foundation upon which a Hash & URL List Database could be built,” the Supreme Court said.

The court added that it was aware that the Sahyog portal currently worked only as a common platform for routing individual reports and takedown notices, and so it acts on CSEAM only when each instance is reported.
However, the portal could do much more, the court said as long as the Union government “shared its vision” with that of the court’s expressed in the present order.

news.story_lead: How day of protests unfolded as disorder breaks out across France - Published 17 October 2026 Violence broke out across France on Saturday during the latest day of demonstrations against hardship in schools and the cost of living. At least 1,200 people were arrested during what the French government described as an "escalation in violence" alongside an estimated 550,000 taking to the streets. In Paris, there were significant clashes into the evening with riot police, who used tear gas and water cannon on crowds.
news.full_article_text: How day of protests unfolded as disorder breaks out across France - Published 17 October 2026 Violence broke out across France on Saturday during the latest day of demonstrations against hardship in schools and the cost of living. At least 1,200 people were arrested during what the French government described as an "escalation in violence" alongside an estimated 550,000 taking to the streets. In Paris, there were significant clashes into the evening with riot police, who used tear gas and water cannon on crowds. Buildings were set alight in the capital and other areas, including in Limoges where a large fire in the town hall caused the roof to partly collapse. La Barrique bar in Paris was set on fire Prime Minister SÃ©bastien Lecornu said 150 police officers were injured in the unrest. Shops were ransacked, at least one restaurant was gutted by fire, and the BBC saw fighting breaking out among some of the groups. Riot police were seen charging at one crowd in central Paris and hitting several people with batons. A car was set alight at the Place de la RÃ©publique in Paris In Lyon, Mayor GrÃ©gory Doucet said the burning of the city's tourist office was "a tragedy" for the city, telling BFMTV "it breaks our hearts because it's a very iconic, well-known historic building". Local police said "hostile individuals" prevented firefighters from safely tackling the blaze. Fire crews also battled the fire at Limoges town hall, which the local prefecture said caused part of the building to collapse. Limoges town hall was "largely lost" in a blaze, the prefecture said A young man "had his hand blown off by a grenade" in Saint-Ãtienne, the south-eastern city's Mayor RÃ©gis Juanico said on social media, adding: "Such a tragedy should never have happened." These groups include the so-called gilets jaunes 'yellow vest' movement, who demonstrated against cost-of-living hikes for over a year from 2018 - becoming one of the longest-lived protest movements in French history. French President Emmanuel Macron will leave office next year and polls suggest April's presidential election could come down to a fight between the leader of the National Rally, Marine Le Pen, and Jean-Luc MÃ©lenchon of the hard-left La France Insoumise party. news.headline: Deferred 100% US tariffs offer only temporary relief to India as Russian oil imports fall
news.story_lead: Deferred 100% US tariffs offer only temporary relief to India as Russian oil imports fall Refiners began reducing their exposure while the bill was still moving through Congress, before Trump signed the Russia and Iran Sanctions act into a law. Washington’s decision to hold off tariffs of up to 100% that a new US sanctions law would have triggered against India for buying Russian oil offers only temporary relief, people familiar with the matter said, as Indian refiners have already cut their Russian purchases and are paying more for the oil that replaced them. Imports of discounted Russian crude have fallen by a third since July, industry executives said, and India’s crude import bill rose 31.6% in September from August even though volumes grew only 14.2%, according to the petroleum ministry’s Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC).
news.full_article_text: Deferred 100% US tariffs offer only temporary relief to India as Russian oil imports fall Refiners began reducing their exposure while the bill was still moving through Congress, before Trump signed the Russia and Iran Sanctions act into a law. Washington’s decision to hold off tariffs of up to 100% that a new US sanctions law would have triggered against India for buying Russian oil offers only temporary relief, people familiar with the matter said, as Indian refiners have already cut their Russian purchases and are paying more for the oil that replaced them. Imports of discounted Russian crude have fallen by a third since July, industry executives said, and India’s crude import bill rose 31.6% in September from August even though volumes grew only 14.2%, according to the petroleum ministry’s Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC). Refiners began reducing their exposure while the bill was still moving through Congress , before US President Donald Trump signed the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act (Graham Act) into law on September 18, company executives and industry experts said on condition of anonymity. They expected geopolitical conditions and the approaching US midterm elections to make it difficult for Washington to enforce the act from October 18, but stepped up imports from the US and other suppliers anyway. Also Read | Indian refiners de-risked in advance, Trump's Russia sanctions waiver a ‘temporary’ relief: Experts Imports of Russian crude have dropped to about 1.8 million barrels a day from around 2.7 million at the July peak, they said. Russian oil made up a negligible share of India’s crude imports until 2021-22. Its share rose to nearly a third in 2025-26, as Moscow, hit by Western sanctions, offered steep discounts. Refiners have replaced it with crude from the US, West Africa, South America and traditional West Asian suppliers, which costs more, partly because of higher freight and insurance charges, they said. Rising Costs and Import Bill In absolute terms, the import bill rose 31.6% in just one month to $15.4 billion in September from $11.7 billion in August, while volumes rose to 21.7 million tonnes from 19 million tonnes (a 14.21% increase), PPAC data show. In this period, average crude oil price of Indian basket increased by 28.71% from $90.19 a barrel in August 2026 to $116.09 per barrel in September 2026. Over April-September 2026-27, the crude import bill rose 46.4% to $90.6 billion, a period that also captured the surge in global oil prices after shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted. Also Read | Republican lawmaker hits out at Trump over Russia sanctions waiver, says he is 'prolonging the war, not ending it' Temporary Relief and Trade Leverage Experts attributed the higher bill to volatile global oil prices, driven by worsening geopolitical tensions, and to the threat the Graham Act posed to major energy importers such as India and China . That threat remains because the act’s secondary sanctions have only been deferred, they said, leaving Trump free to use the law against these countries whenever he chooses. The experts said the waiver offers no long-term assurance either for India’s energy security or for its trade talks with the US, in which New Delhi is seeking a comparative tariff advantage for Indian goods over competing countries. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that the first tranche of the trade agreement would be put into operation once India secured a “competitive advantage” over its peers. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), a New Delhi-based trade think tank, said the US Trade Representative’s continued monitoring of Russian energy purchases would allow “Washington to review the waiver and retain the tariff threat as leverage in future negotiations”. “Under its October 9 agreement with Russia, the US decided to buy Russian diesel to ease domestic shortages and high fuel prices. Punishing other countries for buying Russian energy while doing so itself would invite accusations of double standards. Washington had also agreed not to raise tariffs on China until January 10 under a deal reached during President Xi Jinping’s US visit last month. With US spared, and China shielded, targeting India alone could derail ongoing bilateral trade negotiations,” he said. Also Read | 'Reward for Putin': Zelensky fears US sanctions relief to Russia, diesel deal not the end of it The message was clear, Srivastava said: US interests determined when penalties applied. “For India, the waiver buys time but offers no lasting certainty. Russia’s share of Indian oil imports fell from 51% in July to 44% in August as India bought more from the US, despite higher prices, and from the UAE. Yet SRIA [the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act] remains law, leaving Washington free to revive the tariff threat to extract concessions in bilateral trade talks,” he said. “India should protect its energy security, buy oil on commercial terms and prepare for renewed US pressure. Temporary tariff relief is no basis for permanent trade concessions,” he added. Refiners have replaced it with crude from the US, West Africa, South America and traditional West Asian suppliers, which costs more, partly because of higher freight and insurance charges, they said. Rising Costs and Import Bill In absolute terms, the import bill rose 31.6% in just one month to $15.4 billion in September from $11.7 billion in August, while volumes rose to 21.7 million tonnes from 19 million tonnes (a 14.21% increase), PPAC data show. In this period, average crude oil price of Indian basket increased by 28.71% from $90.19 a barrel in August 2026 to $116.09 per barrel in September 2026. Over April-September 2026-27, the crude import bill rose 46.4% to $90.6 billion, a period that also captured the surge in global oil prices after shipping through the Strait of Hormuz was disrupted. Also Read | Republican lawmaker hits out at Trump over Russia sanctions waiver, says he is 'prolonging the war, not ending it' Temporary Relief and Trade Leverage Experts attributed the higher bill to volatile global oil prices, driven by worsening geopolitical tensions, and to the threat the Graham Act posed to major energy importers such as India and China . That threat remains because the act’s secondary sanctions have only been deferred, they said, leaving Trump free to use the law against these countries whenever he chooses. The experts said the waiver offers no long-term assurance either for India’s energy security or for its trade talks with the US, in which New Delhi is seeking a comparative tariff advantage for Indian goods over competing countries. Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that the first tranche of the trade agreement would be put into operation once India secured a “competitive advantage” over its peers. Ajay Srivastava, founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), a New Delhi-based trade think tank, said the US Trade Representative’s continued monitoring of Russian energy purchases would allow “Washington to review the waiver and retain the tariff threat as leverage in future negotiations”. “Under its October 9 agreement with Russia, the US decided to buy Russian diesel to ease domestic shortages and high fuel prices. Punishing other countries for buying Russian energy while doing so itself would invite accusations of double standards. Washington had also agreed not to raise tariffs on China until January 10 under a deal reached during President Xi Jinping’s US visit last month. With US spared, and China shielded, targeting India alone could derail ongoing bilateral trade negotiations,” he said. Russia’s share of Indian oil imports fell from 51% in July to 44% in August as India bought more from the US, despite higher prices, and from the UAE. Yet SRIA [the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act] remains law, leaving Washington free to revive the tariff threat to extract concessions in bilateral trade talks,” he said. “India should protect its energy security, buy oil on commercial terms and prepare for renewed US pressure. news.headline: Judicial-Led SIT to Probe Kolkata Pandal Stampede; State and Central Relief Packages Announced
news.story_lead: At least 19 people were killed and 25 injured in a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Maha Saptami evening. The West Bengal government has announced a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe headed by a sitting Calcutta High Court judge. Financial compensation and support measures have been announced by both the state and central governments.
news.full_article_text:
### Overview of the Incident
On the evening of Saturday, October 17, 2026 (Maha Saptami), a tragic stampede occurred at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata. The incident resulted in the loss of at least 19 lives and left 25 people injured. Severe overcrowding, unexpected heavy rain, and a sudden rush following an announcement made by the organisers triggered the incident as people waiting outside surged forward.

### Judicial Probe & Investigative Action
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced that a Special Investigation Team (SIT) headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta High Court will investigate the tragedy. The state government will formally request the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court to nominate the sitting judge. The SIT will comprise personnel from the Special Task Force (STF), the Criminal Investigation Department (CID), and other state departments.

The Anti-Rowdy Section of the Kolkata Police has secured CCTV footage to reconstruct the exact sequence of events. Authorities have detained several puja committee members, private security personnel, and duty staff for questioning to determine responsibility for crowd-management failures.

### Compensation and Relief Measures
- **State Government Assistance:** The West Bengal government announced ₹25 lakh compensation and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased individual. Injured victims will receive ₹5 lakh each, with full medical expenses covered at any hospital of their choice.
- **Central Relief Assistance:** Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced ex-gratia relief from the Prime Minister's National Relief Fund (PMNRF) consisting of ₹2 lakh for the next of kin of each deceased person and ₹50,000 for each injured person.
- **Emergency Helplines:** The state government activated a toll-free helpline (1800-345-5678) and Kolkata Police established a dedicated control room helpline (033-2214-1310) for assistance.

### Crowd Control & Safety Directives
To mitigate further safety risks, authorities advised popular theme-based pandals across Kolkata to temporarily suspend visits. Kolkata hosts approximately 3,500 Durga Puja pandals annually, requiring extensive crowd management during peak festival days.

### घटना का विवरण
शनिवार, 17 अक्टूबर 2026 (महा सप्तमी) की शाम उत्तर कोलकाता स्थित चोरबगान सार्वजनीन दुर्गा पूजा पंडाल में एक दुखद भगदड़ घटी। इस हादसे में कम से कम 19 लोगों की जान चली गई और 25 लोग घायल हो गए। भारी भीड़, अचानक आई बारिश और आयोजकों की ओर से की गई एक घोषणा के बाद बाहर खड़े लोग अचानक आगे बढ़े, जिससे यह हादसा हुआ।

### न्यायिक जांच और प्रशासनिक कार्रवाई
पश्चिम बंगाल के मुख्यमंत्री सुवेंदु अधिकारी ने घोषणा की कि कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय के वर्तमान न्यायाधीश की अध्यक्षता में एक विशेष जांच दल (SIT) इस हादसे की जांच करेगा। राज्य सरकार कलकत्ता उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश से इसके लिए न्यायाधीश नामित करने का अनुरोध करेगी। SIT में स्पेशल टास्क फोर्स (STF), आपराधिक जांच विभाग (CID) और अन्य विभागों के अधिकारी शामिल होंगे।

कोलकाता पुलिस के एंटी-राउडी सेक्शन ने घटनाक्रम को समझने के लिए सीसीटीवी फुटेज जब्त कर ली है। भीड़ प्रबंधन में चूक के संबंध में पूछताछ के लिए पूजा समिति के सदस्यों, निजी सुरक्षा गार्डों और ड्यूटी पर तैनात कर्मियों को हिरासत में लिया गया है।

### मुआवजा और राहत उपाय
- **राज्य सरकार की सहायता:** पश्चिम बंगाल सरकार ने मृतक के परिजनों को ₹25 लाख का मुआवजा और एक ग्रुप डी सरकारी नौकरी देने की घोषणा की। घायलों को ₹5 लाख की सहायता और उनकी पसंद के अस्पताल में मुफ्त इलाज की सुविधा मिलेगी।
- **केंद्रीय राहत सहायता:** प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने प्रधानमंत्री राष्ट्रीय राहत कोष (PMNRF) से प्रत्येक मृतक के परिजन को ₹2 लाख और घायलों को ₹50,000 की अनुग्रह राशि देने की घोषणा की।
- **आपातकालीन हेल्पलाइन:** राज्य सरकार ने एक टोल-फ्री हेल्पलाइन (1800-345-5678) और कोलकाता पुलिस ने एक कंट्रोल रूम हेल्पलाइन (033-2214-1310) जारी की है।

### भीड़ नियंत्रण और सुरक्षा निर्देश
सुरक्षा जोखिमों को देखते हुए अधिकारियों ने कोलकाता के लोकप्रिय थीम-आधारित पंडालों को अस्थायी रूप से बंद करने की सलाह दी है। कोलकाता में प्रतिवर्ष लगभग 3,500 दुर्गा पूजा पंडाल लगाए जाते हैं।

SIT में CID, STF और राज्य के अन्य संबंधित विभागों के अधिकारी शामिल होंगे।
राज्य सरकार ने मृतकों के परिवारों को ₹25 लाख व नौकरी और घायलों को ₹5 लाख व मुफ्त इलाज देने की घोषणा की।
PMNRF से मृतकों के परिजनों को ₹2 लाख और घायलों को ₹50,000 की सहायता प्रदान की जाएगी।

quiz.question: What is the financial compensation announced by the West Bengal government for the families of those who died in the Kolkata pandal stampede?
options: ₹10 lakh and a Group C job
₹25 lakh and a Group D job
quiz.correct_answer: ₹25 lakh and a Group D job

news.story_lead: 'Swelling crowd, situation worsened by rain': What we know so far about Kolkata pandal stampede The stampede took place at Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity puja pandal, a prominent puja in central Kolkata, during the peak hours on Saturday evening. Durga Puja festivities in Kolkata turned tragic on Saturday after a stampede-like situation left at least 17 dead , while several others are said to be injured. The incident took place at Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity puja pandal, a prominent puja in central Kolkata, during the peak hours on Saptami evening, police said.
news.full_article_text: 'Swelling crowd, situation worsened by rain': What we know so far about Kolkata pandal stampede The stampede took place at Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity puja pandal, a prominent puja in central Kolkata, during the peak hours on Saturday evening. Durga Puja festivities in Kolkata turned tragic on Saturday after a stampede-like situation left at least 17 dead , while several others are said to be injured. The incident took place at Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durgotsab Samity puja pandal, a prominent puja in central Kolkata, during the peak hours on Saptami evening, police said. Track live updates on Kolkata stampede While the exact cause of the crowd crush is yet to be ascertained, eyewitnesses said that the surging crowd and rainfall worsened the situation. “The incident took place around 7:30 pm. The crowd at the pandal was already swelling. As it started to rain more people entered the pandal. This resulted in a stampede. Several people were injured,” Dipali Das, a pandal hopper, told the media. Deep Dive Another eyewitness alleged mismanagement and said that people pushing each other in absence of organisers, volunteers and police personnel. “There were no puja organsier, no police and no volunteer. Everyone was pushing each other and shouting. Many fell ill,” said Saikat Banerjee, another pandal hopper. Also read: Kolkata pandal stampede: Mamata Banerjee expresses 'shock and grief', TMC alleges poor crowd management As leaders expressed grief over the loss of lives in the Kolkata pandal stampede, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced ₹ 2 lakh ex-gratia to next of kin of each deceased and ₹ 50,000 for injured. “Stampede in Kolkata extremely distressing; my thoughts with people who have lost loved ones,” PM Modi said. Meanwhile, Union home minister Amit Shah Union is expected to visit injured in hospitals on Sunday, news agency PTI reported. What the authorities said The incident occurred at around 7:40 pm, and the pandal has now been closed to visitors, news agency ANI reported, citing Kolkata Police. "Today at around 7:40 pm, a stampede occurred at the exit gate of Sarada Park (Chor Bagan) Puja Pandal, under Girish Park Police Station, due to heavy crowds of pandal hoppers amid rainfall. The Puja Pandal has now been closed to visitors. All injured persons were rescued and shifted to MCH for treatment," the police said. West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari and chief secretary Manoj Agarwal visited the hospitalised injured at Calcutta Medical College and Hospital. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Joydeep Thakur Joydeep Thakur is a Special Correspondent based in Kolkata. news.headline: Indore BJP official booked under POCSO for misbehaving with girl at Garba venue
news.story_lead: Indore BJP official booked under POCSO for misbehaving with girl at Garba venue Accused Kamal Chauhan is a supporter of MLA Ramesh Mendola and was assigned duty to manage arrangements at the Garba venue at Kankeshwari Ground in Indore. BJP mandal president Kamal Chauhan, who allegedly pushed and misbehaved with a 15-year-old girl at a Garba venue, was booked under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and molestation charges in Indore on Saturday. Chauhan is a supporter of MLA Ramesh Mendola.
news.full_article_text: Indore BJP official booked under POCSO for misbehaving with girl at Garba venue Accused Kamal Chauhan is a supporter of MLA Ramesh Mendola and was assigned duty to manage arrangements at the Garba venue at Kankeshwari Ground in Indore. BJP mandal president Kamal Chauhan, who allegedly pushed and misbehaved with a 15-year-old girl at a Garba venue, was booked under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and molestation charges in Indore on Saturday. Chauhan is a supporter of MLA Ramesh Mendola. He was assigned duty to manage arrangements at the Garba venue at Kankeshwari Ground in Indore. The party has also taken cognizance after the video of the incident went viral and served a show cause notice. The party state president Hemant Khandelwal asked him to reply within three days. Heeranagar town inspector KK Sharma said the minor girl from Khatipura had filed complaint against Kamal Chauhan. “On Thursday night, the girl had gone to watch Garba. Her elder sister was performing Garba and when she went to give her a pass, Kamal picked up an argument and pushed her out aggressively. The entire incident happened in front of the girl's family members,” said the TI. A video of it went viral on social media. Taking cognizance, police on Saturday recorded the girl's statement and registered an FIR against Chauhan. However, Chauhan said his intention was not to misbehave with the girl. “It happened while managing the pandal after argument heated up with the family for taking entry with pass.”

news.headline: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD
news.story_lead: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force arrested a government doctor and two others after busting an alleged mephedrone manufacturing unit in Balotra. A government doctor was among three people arrested after Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted an alleged mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit at a house in Balotra district on Saturday. Police seized 3.764 kg of raw MD, chemicals and equipment, ₹ 3.41 lakh in cash and a car.
news.full_article_text: Government doctor among 3 arrested as Rajasthan ANTF seizes 3.764 kg of raw MD Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force arrested a government doctor and two others after busting an alleged mephedrone manufacturing unit in Balotra. A government doctor was among three people arrested after Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) busted an alleged mephedrone (MD) manufacturing unit at a house in Balotra district on Saturday. Police seized 3.764 kg of raw MD, chemicals and equipment, ₹ 3.41 lakh in cash and a car. The ANTF team, with assistance from local police, raided the premises in the Siwana police station area after receiving information about an alleged MD manufacturing unit, deputy inspector general of police Abhijeet Singh said. Police identified the three arrested men as prime suspect Suresh Kumar Vishnoi (27), a resident of Mithora; Dr Mukesh Vishnoi (29), and Utkarsh Vishnoi (19), a resident of Modran village in Jalore district. From failed government job aspirant to alleged MD manufacturer Suresh completed his graduation and attempted several government recruitment examinations, including those for patwari, gram sevak, Rajasthan Police, forest guard and police sub-inspector posts, but failed to secure a government job, an ANTF officer said. In 2022, he moved to Bengaluru with a friend and began working in pharmaceutical sales as a medical representative. After working in the field for around two years, he allegedly found the earnings insufficient. Police said Suresh returned to his village in 2024 and came into contact with people involved in drug trafficking. He allegedly began purchasing, selling and supplying MD before deciding to manufacture it himself in pursuit of higher profits. Investigators suspect that he learnt the process of manufacturing MD by watching videos on YouTube and other social media platforms. He allegedly used chemicals and equipment to prepare the drug at his house in Mithora. According to the ANTF, Suresh had called Dr Mukesh Vishnoi and Utkarsh Vishnoi to his house to sell a consignment of MD. The two allegedly arrived in a car. Police suspect that Suresh used Dr Mukesh’s contacts to supply the drug in and around Jalore and Siwana. During questioning, Suresh allegedly disclosed details about supplying MD through his associates and other people involved in drug trafficking. Raw MD, chemicals and equipment seized The ANTF team had received information that Suresh was operating an MD manufacturing unit at his house and in the adjoining premises. After verifying the information, the team conducted a raid with local police. Officers said that the three men were found sitting in a shed outside the house. A search of the house and surrounding premises led to the recovery of raw MD, chemicals and equipment allegedly used to manufacture and dry the drug. All three were arrested, and the seized material was taken into custody. The seized material included 3.764 kg of raw MD, including its packaging, and two packets of powder allegedly used in manufacturing the drug, weighing 888 grams including the plastic bags. Police also seized 800 grams of methylene dichloride (MDC) and 514 grams of a chemical described in the seizure details as isopropyl acid. The equipment recovered from the premises included an electric churning machine, an induction cooktop, a large glass jar, a thermometer and a piece of cloth bearing a substance allegedly used in drying MD. In addition, the team seized ₹ 3,41,700 in cash and a Kia Seltos bearing registration number RJ-19-CT-10351.

news.headline: Brazil sees record fall in Amazon deforestation as key election looms
news.story_lead: - Published 17 October 2026, 03:33 BST Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue. Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro.
news.full_article_text: - Published 17 October 2026, 03:33 BST Brazil's government says deforestation rates in the country's Amazon and savanna regions have fallen to record lows ahead of a presidential election run-off in which the rainforest's future is a key issue. Left-wing President Luiz InÃ¡cio Lula da Silva, when he assumed office three years ago, pledged to end deforestation by 2030 in the Amazon. It had surged under his right-wing predecessor, Jair Bolsonaro. Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon. Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%. The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil. Why the Amazon rainforest is so important What in the World podcast Jair Bolsonaro promoted mining in indigenous lands in the Amazon and forest clearances soared at the same time as resources to protect the forest were cut. During Bolsonaro's presidency from 2019 to 2022, the Amazon lost nearly 60% more in forest lands compared to the previous four years, news agency AFP reported, citing official data. Lula reversed his policies and oversaw deforestation rates drop to a six-year low during his first year in office. Lula tightened up environmental monitoring and penalties for illegal logging. "Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he said in a post on X on Friday. Tropical rainforests like the Amazon are home to millions of species. In a healthy state, they absorb vast quantities of planet-warming carbon dioxide, helping to keep the Earth cool. But they have come under increasing pressure from decades of deliberate land clearance for agriculture and logging, as well as climate change, which scientists warn can create conditions for wildfires. Brazil's Environment Minister Joao Paulo Capobianco described the decline in Amazon deforestation as "absolutely stratospheric". It was an "historic achievement" for Brazil, said Marcio Astrini, executive secretary at climate advocacy group Observatorio do Clima. It showed that "with political will, it is possible to curb deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions", Astrini said. Lula will face Bolsonaro's son Flavio in the run-off on 25 October, with polls suggesting a neck-and-neck race. Flavio is expected to continue his father's policies if he wins, though he has pledged to fight organised crime in the Amazon.

Satellite data shows that in the year to July 2026, the deforestation rate fell by 41.8% in the Amazon - the biggest drop since records began in 1988. The fall in the Cerrado, Brazil's savanna region, was 23.8%.
The Amazon rainforest - the world's largest - is a crucial buffer in the global fight against climate change and 60% of it is located in Brazil.

news.full_article_text: HT Evening Brief October 17: Abhijeet Dipke gets conditional bail; Supreme Court backs children’s internet rights Here's a quick recap of the day's top headlines from India, the world and the field of sports and entertainment. Good evening! Here's your 5-minute wrap of the day's top headlines from across the country and the world. Abhijeet Dipke granted conditional bail upon signing peace bond CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke was granted conditional bail on Saturday, a day after he was detained on his way to Connaught Place and subsequently arrested. Dipke has been released by the special executive magistrate subject to a conditional bail bond. One of the primary conditions would be to ensure there is no breach of peace on his end for a period of one year. Read more here . ‘Children have fundamental right to internet access’: Supreme Court The right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right of every individual, including children irrespective of their age, the Supreme Court has held, cautioning that blanket restrictions on children’s internet access in the name of safety risk undermining their freedom, privacy and ability to seek help when they encounter online abuse. Read more here . US Congressman claims H-1B holders from India, China replacing Americans US Congressman Riley Moore has alleged that H-1 B visa holders are replacing American computer science graduates, claiming employers are turning to foreign workers willing to accept lower wages. In a post on X accompanying a snippet of his television interview, Moore called the H-1B and Optional Practical Training (OPT) programmes “SCAMS” and alleged that they undercut and replace American workers with cheaper foreign labour. Read more here . Yashasvi Jaiswal's non-selection for New Zealand ODIs unfair: R Ashwin Former India off-spinner R Ashwin was displeased when Yashasvi Jaiswal was omitted from the squad for the upcoming five-match ODI series against New Zealand, beginning November 4. The BCCI announced the squads for the ODI and Test assignments on Friday evening, and Jaiswal didn't make the cut despite Shubman Gill not being a part of the team for the final two ODIs. Read more here . Legendary music composer Deva dies at 75 Legendary music composer Deva died on October 17 at the age of 75. The man who composed the famous intro music that Rajinikanth now uses in all his films suffered a heart attack and was admitted to a private hospital before his death. Khushbu Sundar expressed shock at the news, having met the composer just 10 days before his death. The team also leads coverage of major breaking news events, policy announcements, court proceedings, natural disasters, public emergencies and significant international developments. Read more here . The man who composed the famous intro music that Rajinikanth now uses in all his films suffered a heart attack and was admitted to a private hospital before his death. Khushbu Sundar expressed shock at the news, having met the composer just 10 days before his death.
